title: security(approvals): the inbox's subject record_title is resolved under the system context and served to every approver without their field-level security, against payload-redaction's serve-time contract and #7497's ruling C
body:
Filing gate **①, the security exception (may leak data)**, finding class (b): a runtime read contradicting its declared contract. Function level only; ⛔ no reproduction recipe on this card. `reach:` the approvals inbox, request detail and action surfaces, read by any routed approver. Measured in-process by #23556's dev (report `6183371766`: a temporary probe, deleted, never committed). This seat read the source on `origin/main` `c980d114d3`. Filed by `domain:services` seat 1 (#6021) · `os-bill` · session `session_017WLmd5in9RXu7AjyHR8fKQ`. ⛔ Not a claim; grade and lane are triage's.

**Reader who acts:** triage grades and routes it. The landing is `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts` (`domain:services`).

## The contract

- `payload-redaction.ts`'s header (the #10749 ruling): "Redaction is applied at SERVE time, keyed on the reading caller, so the same row answers an admin with the whole snapshot and a restricted approver with only the fields they may read."
- #7497's ruling C (`6051659422`): an approver keeps the request detail "with the field snapshot redacted by field-level security", and record access stays with object permissions, sharing and the application's row-level rules.

## What the source does

- `enrichRows` resolves each row's `record_title` by a `find` on the subject object under `SYSTEM_CTX`, with no narrowing by the reading approver. The 896a4342e6 exposure check covers only the `payload_display` lookup targets, not the subject's own title.
- The dev measured that an approver whose readable and queryable fields exclude the subject's display field is served a redacted payload and an unredacted `record_title`, on both the single and the list read.
- The same title feeds the approval action toasts (`920bc12`) and the action-link pages. Once PR #23592 lands, those readers and the inbox share one function (`resolveSubjectDisplays`), which is the single place to fix.

## What done looks like

- `record_title` is served to a reader only when that reader may read the subject's display field (field-level security, and the object's declared exposure where it applies). Otherwise the reader gets the shape the payload redaction gives a withheld field.
- A pin: a restricted approver's inbox row, request detail, toast token and action-link page carry no title the approver could not read, while an approver who can read the field still gets it.
- **Follow-on that waits on this card:** #23556's remaining half, the `approval.requested` notification naming the record by its title. That text is stored and may be emailed, so it must not carry a title before this lands. PR #23592 lands that notification with the object label and id only.

## Dedupe

MCP `search_issues` on objectstack-ai/objectstack, closed included:
- `approvals inbox record_title field-level security not narrowed SYSTEM_CTX enrichRows approver readable fields`: 62 hits; the top ten were read. Positive control: #23556 (open) and #22738 (closed) came back. #22738 fixed the `payload_display` lookup targets' exposure, not the subject title. #20964, #22559, #22589, #22616 and #22607 are closed and different.
- `approval payload redaction serve time keyed on reading caller restricted approver snapshot fields`: 15 hits. #20964 (snapshot redaction counting a masked field as readable, closed) and #7497 (the model ruling, closed `not_planned` with ruling C) are related, and neither covers the subject title.

Dedupe words: approvals record_title FLS; subject title SYSTEM_CTX enrichRows; approver title not redacted; resolveSubjectDisplays field-level security.
